use_case_name: Publish Air and Surface Surveillance Tracks

claims.content: To transmit and receive all the response values of the J7.2 message for real-time air and/or surface tracks, which are held locally by their system.

goal.raw_text: To transmit and receive all the response values of the J7.2 message for real-time air and/or surface tracks, which are held locally by their system.

claims.content: C2 JU
The C² JU must be capable of reporting air or surface tracks.
The C² JU must have the capability to transmit and receive all the response values of the J7.2 message for real-time air and/or surface tracks, which are held locally by their system.
The C² JU must have an automatic correlation capability if it originates real-time air or surface tracks.
The C² JU must have locally derived sensor data (position, velocity, and altitude) for comparison with received interface data to prevent or eliminate dual designations.
A system does not receive a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message and receives no further updates on the remote track.

trigger.raw_text: A system does not receive a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message and receives no further updates on the remote track.

claims.content: The C² JU compares locally derived sensor data (position, velocity, and altitude) with data received on the interface to prevent or eliminate dual designations.
If a track for which positional data has been locally derived by a C² JU is currently being reported by another C² JU, it is referred to as a 'common local track'.
All C² JUs perform correlation and decorrelation of their local track data with respect to the remote data they are receiving to ensure common tracking functions properly.
The C² JU reports the position of a real-time track extrapolated to the time of transmission.
Nonreal-time data is identified as such and time tags are provided; nonreal-time track positions are not extrapolated.
The source of track data is provided via Source TN in the transmitted message.
Track reporting ensures that information on the track is as complete, accurate, and timely as possible.
Data are correlated and dual designation is minimized during track reporting.
Proper rules for reporting a track are followed according to system configuration and operational requirements.
If the Dropped TN Mode IV data is a higher value than the Retained TN Mode IV data, it shall be transferred to the Retained TN.
If the Dropped TN had the Force Tell Indicator set to value 1, the Retained TN shall have the Force Tell Indicator set to value 1.
If the Dropped TN had the Emergency Indicator set to value 1, the Retained TN shall have the Emergency Indicator set to value 1.

Common local tracks shall be decorrelated if, on receipt of 2(1-5, 1) consecutive remote track reports, the remote track falls outside a distance of 1.5(1.0-2.0, 0.1) times the maximum correlation distance calculated in accordance with paragraph 4.4.4.3.1f(3).
The local track shall be automatically tested once for correlation against remote tracks (not common local tracks) in accordance with paragraphs 4.4.4.3.1f and g.
If the automatic correlation test fails, assign a new TN (TN B) to the local track and report TN B in a J3.2 or J3.3 message.

When a C² JU recognizes that two tracks which are being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation, that JU shall initiate action, either automatically or manually, to resolve the dual designation.
The recognizing JU shall transmit the J7.2 Correlation message requesting all other C² IUs to perform a correlation of the two tracks.

The receiving IUs shall accept the requested correlation unless certain prespecified conditions exist which require or allow the receiving IU to reject the requested correlation or respond with a reverse correlation request.
When the RV field is set to value 0 it indicates a reverse correlation would be acceptable, and when the RV field is set to value 1 it indicates a reverse correlation request would be rejected.
Whenever a correlation request is rejected the J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 shall be transmitted to report the rejection.
When the RV field is set to value 3, it indicates the correlation was manually initiated and shall be accepted unless certain conditions apply which require rejection.

If the C² JU recognizes that two tracks are eligible for correlation and initiates a J7.2 Correlation message, receiving IUs may reject the requested correlation or respond with a reverse correlation request if certain prespecified conditions exist.
When the RV field in the J7.2 message is set to value 1, it indicates that a reverse correlation request would be rejected by the originating JU.
Whenever a correlation request is rejected, the J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 shall be transmitted to report the rejection.

If the RV field is set to value 3 (indicating manually initiated correlation), the correlation shall be accepted unless certain conditions apply which require rejection — implying an exception path exists even for manual correlations under specific constraints.

After initially achieving Active status, or after returning to Active status from Inactive status or TDS Failure, C² JUs capable of assuming R² for air, surface, or land tracks shall not transmit those tracks until sufficient reporting responsibility checks, correlation, and data registration are performed — failure to complete these steps constitutes an exception preventing track publication.

The minimum wait before reporting air and surface tracks is 12 seconds; for land tracks it is 60 seconds. If operational necessity requires shorter wait times or none at all, system design must allow override — otherwise, premature transmission without meeting timing constraints constitutes an exception condition.

All C² JUs capable of reporting air or surface tracks have transmitted and received all the response values of the J7.2 message for real-time air and/or surface tracks, which are held locally by their system.

Dual designations between remote and local tracks (and optionally common local tracks) have been resolved through periodic comparison and correlation rules in accordance with section 4.4.4.3.1, Air and Surface Track Correlation.
Correlation requests initiated via J7.2 messages have been either accepted, rejected (with RV=2), or responded to with reverse correlation (RV=0 or RV=1) as per prespecified conditions.
Manually initiated correlations (indicated by RV=3) have been accepted unless certain conditions apply which require rejection.
Tracks published include validated identity, position, velocity, strength, and source TN; nonreal-time data is identified with time tags and not extrapolated.
Minimum wait times before transmitting tracks (12 seconds for air/surface, 60 seconds for land) have been observed unless overridden by operational necessity.
